key_test: paired t-test, two-sided: per-subject mean localization error (angle, deg) on test-phase distractor-centroid trials (one_vs_four=4, tar_vs_dis=11) vs guessing-phase four-missing trials (ExGuess=guessing, one_vs_four=4); dz = t/sqrt(n)
variables: angle (route B: v2,v4,v7-v10,v12-v19 from raw txt)
exclusions: none at participant level; trial selection only (680 of 2040 trials)

r_script.why_not: package missing: readstata13, doBy, lsr (and httr, RCurl) not installed; the script also sources sachaepskamp.com, outside the allowed hosts

agreement: table and Python agree (t -9.59 vs -9.591, dz -2.33 vs -2.326; table p 1e-04 is a floor, exact p 4.9e-8); R script not run
notes: Route A uses the posted .dta's angle. Route B rebuilds angle from the 17 raw MATLAB txt files (files 1-2 have a v1..v19 header, 3-17 none) following 'merge and analyze.do'. Emulating the do-file exactly reproduces every trial's angle (max diff 4e-6) and the same t. Surprise: the do-file orders the quadrilateral's corners by slope from the leftmost point but gives that point a sentinel slope of -50, so a corner with slope below -50 sorts ahead of it and the centroid is computed on a self-crossing polygon. This hits 2 trials (subject 5: experimental trial 25, guessing trial 24); with the geometrically correct ordering, t(16) = -9.668, p = 4.4e-8, dz = -2.345. Negligible for the verdict. Means: test phase 2.845 deg, guessing 7.549 deg (report: distractor centroid M=2.84; guessing four-missing M=7.56).
